questions.statement: By the time the computer crashed, I ________ my essay for three hours.
questions.context: Describing the sequence of using a computer.

options.feedback: Incorrect. We need a tense that shows an action in progress before another past action.
Incorrect. This would mean the writing was finished before the crash, but the duration "for three hours" suggests progress.
Correct! Past Perfect Continuous shows an action that was ongoing up to a point in the past.
Incorrect. This is Present Perfect Continuous, but the context is the past ("crashed").

questions.explanation:
El Pasado Perfecto Continuo (*had been writing*) se utiliza para expresar la duración de una acción que estaba en progreso hasta que ocurrió otro evento en el pasado (el fallo del ordenador).

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Valentina was exhausted because she ________ all night to finish the coding project.
questions.context: Explaining why someone was tired after a digital task.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is Simple Past and doesn't emphasize the cause of her state.
Correct! Past Perfect Continuous emphasizes the cause of a state in the past.
Incorrect. This would imply she is still working or just finished now.
Incorrect. This describes what she was doing at a specific time, not the reason for her exhaustion.

questions.explanation:
Usamos el Pasado Perfecto Continuo para hablar de una acción pasada que causó una situación o estado también en el pasado (*was exhausted*), resaltando el esfuerzo prolongado.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Before social media became popular, people ________ emails as their primary way to stay in touch.
questions.context: Sequencing two past events in the history of the internet.

options.feedback: Incorrect. While possible, Past Perfect is better to clearly show which action happened first.
Correct! Past Perfect Simple indicates an action completed before another past event.
Incorrect. Present Perfect cannot be used for a completed past period.
Incorrect. This emphasizes progress but not the sequence as clearly as Past Perfect.

questions.explanation:
El Pasado Perfecto Simple (*had used*) se emplea para clarificar que una acción ocurrió y se completó antes de otro momento o acción en el pasado (*became popular*).

questions.statement:
"Why didn't you join the Zoom meeting yesterday?"
"I couldn't. I ________ with my internet provider for an hour before they fixed the signal."
questions.context: A student explaining why they couldn't join a video call.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Doesn't reflect the sequence and duration well.
Correct! Shows the duration of the struggle before the resolution in the past.
Incorrect. This only shows the action was in progress, but not its relation to the "fixing".
Incorrect. Inappropriate for a specific past context.

questions.explanation:
El Pasado Perfecto Continuo es ideal para describir procesos largos y a veces frustrantes que precedieron a una solución en el pasado.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The hackers ________ to access the database for weeks when the security team finally detected them.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Too simple for an ongoing attempt before a past event.
Incorrect. This would mean they stopped trying before they were detected.
Correct! Highlights the ongoing attempt that was interrupted by detection.
Incorrect. Mixed tenses (present vs past).

questions.explanation:
Este tiempo gramatical es muy útil para describir situaciones de vigilancia o intentos repetidos en el pasado que son interrumpidos por otro evento (*detected*).

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: By 2015, many Colombian artists ________ their music to streaming platforms to reach a global audience.
questions.context: Discussing the evolution of music streaming.

options.feedback: Correct! Past Perfect for a completed action before a specific point in time (*By 2015*).
Incorrect. Present Perfect refers to a time up to now, not a past deadline.
Incorrect. This focuses on the process, not the completion by the date.
Incorrect. Simple Past doesn't show the "before then" relationship.

questions.explanation:
La preposición *By* seguida de una fecha pasada es una señal clara de que debemos usar el Pasado Perfecto para indicar que la acción ya se había realizado antes de ese límite.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence suggests that the digital project was **finished** before the deadline?
questions.context: Comparing Past Perfect Simple and Continuous.

options.text: When the deadline arrived, Juan had already finished the website.
options.feedback: Correct! Past Perfect Simple shows completion.

options.text: When the deadline arrived, Juan had been working on the website.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This implies he was still working on it.

options.text: When the deadline arrived, Juan was finishing the website.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This means he was in the middle of it.

options.text: When the deadline arrived, Juan finished the website.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This suggests he finished it at the same time or just after.

questions.explanation:
El Pasado Perfecto Simple (*had finished*) enfatiza el resultado y la finalización, mientras que el Continuo (*had been working*) enfatiza el proceso y la duración.

questions.statement: "The app didn't work because I ________ the latest update."
questions.context: Understanding causal relationships in technology failure.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Both actions are in Simple Past, which doesn't show the priority.
Correct! The failure to download happened before the app failed to work.
Incorrect. This implies a continuous action that wasn't happening.
Incorrect. Present Perfect doesn't fit the past context of "didn't work".

questions.explanation:
Usamos el Pasado Perfecto para explicar la causa de algo que sucedió después en el pasado. La falta de descarga (*hadn't downloaded*) fue el motivo previo del error.

questions.statement: After the company ________ its new smartphone, they realized that they ________ to include the charger in the box.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Doesn't show the full sequence clearly.
Incorrect. Mixed past and present.
Correct! Both actions happened before the realization.
Incorrect. Doesn't reflect completion.

questions.explanation:
Cuando tenemos una serie de eventos pasados, usamos el Pasado Perfecto para marcar las acciones que ocurrieron antes de la acción principal del relato (*realized*).

questions.statement:
Identify the error in this paragraph:
"Before the first personal computer **appeared** (A), scientists **had already been using** (B) large machines for calculations. These early computers **had occupied** (C) entire rooms and **had required** (D) a lot of electricity."
questions.context: Finding an error in a text about the history of computers.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is the correct past reference point.
Incorrect. This correctly describes the ongoing use before the PC.
Incorrect. This should be Simple Past (*occupied*) because it describes a permanent state/fact of those machines, not a sequence of events.
Incorrect. Similar to C, Simple Past (*required*) is better for general characteristics in the past.

questions.explanation:
No todas las acciones en el pasado necesitan el Pasado Perfecto. Para descripciones de características o estados permanentes en el pasado, el *Simple Past* es la forma estándar.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which explanation is most likely from someone who is **frustrated** by a lost file?
questions.context: Judging the best explanation for a digital mistake.

options.text: I lost the file because I forgot to save it.
options.feedback: Incorrect. A neutral statement of fact.

options.text: I had been working on that file for three hours when the power went out and I lost everything!
options.feedback: Correct! The Past Perfect Continuous emphasizes the wasted effort and time.

options.text: I had already saved the file when the power went out.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This implies the file is safe.

options.text: I have been losing files all day.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Present Perfect doesn't explain the specific past loss as well.

questions.explanation:
A nivel B2, el estudiante debe reconocer que el Pasado Perfecto Continuo no solo indica tiempo, sino que a menudo añade un matiz emocional sobre el esfuerzo invertido en una tarea.

questions.statement: "Before the pandemic started, most companies ________ the idea of remote work, but they soon realized they ________ no choice but to adapt."
questions.context: Choosing the best conclusion for a text about connectivity.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Tenses don't match.
Correct! Rejection happened before the pandemic, and the realization followed.
Incorrect. The sequence is inverted.
Incorrect. "Have" (possession) is a stative verb.

questions.explanation: Esta pregunta requiere evaluar el orden cronológico lógico: primero se rechaza una idea (*had rejected*), luego llega un cambio externo, y finalmente se tiene una necesidad (*had*).
